title: Rebuild Ordio as a premium one-page static website
next_action: Audit the complete existing Ordio website and produce a verified business, content and brand inventory before writing or designing the new page.
goal: Create a modern, premium, conversion-focused one-page static website for Ordio with a complete visual identity, typography system and responsive section-by-section implementation.
instructions: Use https://ordio.au/ and its existing internal pages as the primary source of truth.
Inspect Home, What We Do, Who We Work With, FAQs and Demo before designing.
Do not copy the existing page layout.
Do not fabricate services, client names, testimonials, statistics, certifications, locations or claims.
Preserve useful Ordio brand equity such as its logo, company name, established positioning and recognizable brand cues.
Modernize the visual identity substantially.
Build one section at a time.
Finish and visually review each section before moving to the next section.
After each major build stage, capture a screenshot and inspect the actual rendered page.
Use screenshot evidence to correct typography, spacing, hierarchy and responsiveness.
Maintain one design system across the whole site.
Use semantic HTML and lightweight CSS and JavaScript.
The final deliverable is one static responsive landing page.
Prioritize fast loading, clarity and conversion.
Primary CTA should remain centred around requesting a free demo unless evidence from the existing site supports a better equivalent.
Use Australian Ordio details for the Australian website.
Do not accidentally carry New Zealand contact details into the Australian landing page.
Use verified Australian contact details from the current website.
Do not begin final page construction until the brand direction and typography system are defined.
Treat the redesign as a premium audio and caller-experience brand, not a generic telecom or agency template.
Use audio-inspired visual language where appropriate, such as waveform motifs, sound bars, timeline elements, play controls and subtle motion.
Prefer oversized editorial typography, strong contrast, generous whitespace and restrained animation.
Use sophisticated brand-appropriate imagery rather than generic telecom stock imagery.
Make voice demos a major visual and conversion section rather than a buried secondary feature.
Use the hero direction: Make every caller interaction sound like your brand.
Use supporting copy direction: Professional voice, music and managed caller experiences—from IVR and on-hold messaging to voicemail and voiceovers.
Use Request a Free Demo as the primary CTA.
Use Hear Our Voices as the secondary CTA where appropriate.
